sources.note: Saek used only as a comparative witness (Proto-Tai sesquisyllabic clusters > Saek tr- etc.); no statement on synchronic Saek word stress (a full-text search for stress/accent full text).

sources.citation: Hudak, Thomas John (ed.). 1993. William J. Gedney's The Saek Language: Glossary, Texts, and Translations (Michigan Papers on South and Southeast Asia 41). Ann Arbor: CSSEAS. [Rosetta Project excerpts: Introduction pp. xix-xx, 'Phonology' page, 'Syntax' pp. xxxiii ff.]
sources.note: Excerpted phonology page: 'the phonological pattern of Saek is based on the syllable' with tone (Chao values), consonant and vowel charts only; no stress statement in the excerpt. Remainder of the Introduction (pp. xxi-xxxii) not accessible (HathiTrust search-only, could not be reached by automated download).

sources.citation: Khanittanan, Wilaiwan. 1979. Saek revisited. pp. 109-117 [SEAlang SALA scan].
sources.note: Nothing; word classes (pronouns, particles, classifiers) and vitality; defers phonology to Gedney 1970. Only prosody-adjacent note: first syllable of classifier-noun compounds may be dropped (p. 116). scanned (image-only scan).

sources.citation: Gedney, William J. 1970. The Saek language of Nakhon Phanom Province. Journal of the Siam Society 58(1): 67-87.
sources.note: Nothing. Phonology (pp. 71-77) covers six tones (glottal constriction on tones 3, 6), checked-syllable tones, nine long/short vowels, diphthongs, clusters, final -l, generational variation; no mention of stress/accent (full read + a full-text search for stress/accent).
